# Release watcher: technical specification

Version 1.0.0 of the specification: 3 requirements, 19 tests and 1 environment. The chapters follow arc42, and a chapter with nothing in the specification is left out.

## 1. Introduction and goals

A daemon that asks a registry for new releases of a host's services and
installs them, and a nightly program that prunes old releases. Both run
under systemd; their unit files are in ../sources/units.

### Stakeholders

| Stakeholder | Who they are | Concerns |
|---|---|---|
| host-owner | The person who runs the host and its services. |   |

## 6. Runtime view

### Job sweep

Asks the registry for the latest release of each service and installs one newer than the installed.

Runs every PT1M, as the role installer. Running it twice over the same records changes nothing a second time.

### Job prune

Removes the releases of each service older than its last three.

Runs on the schedule `0 3 * * *` (UTC), as the role installer. Running it twice over the same records changes nothing a second time.

### Process releaseWatcher

Asks the registry for a new release of each service and installs it.

**Origin:** stated in The systemd units of the release watcher, clause release-watcher.service.

**Note:** From The systemd units of the release watcher, clause release-watcher.service: Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=5s, StartLimitBurst=5 within StartLimitIntervalSec=10min, RestartPreventExitStatus=78, TimeoutStopSec=30s, WatchdogSec=2min, ExecReload sends SIGHUP. <../sources/units>

Runs always, from the host's start; started and watched by the service manager, acting as no role. Runs the jobs sweep. Reads the settings registryAddress, registryToken and logLevel when it starts. On SIGTERM: finishes the release it is installing, then exits 0, within PT30S; on SIGHUP: reads its settings again. Exits 0 when it was asked to stop; 78 when a setting is missing or wrong. Started again: when it fails, after PT5S; given up after 5 starts within PT10M. Never started again after exit 78. Healthy when it has asked the registry within the last two minutes, and tells the service manager so. Watched by watcher-running.

### Process releasePrune

Removes old releases each night.

**Origin:** stated in The systemd units of the release watcher, clause release-prune.timer.

**Note:** From The systemd units of the release watcher, clause release-prune.timer: OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:00:00 on a host whose clock is UTC, which the job prune's schedule says. <../sources/units>

Runs when a job it runs is due; started and watched by the service manager, acting as no role. Runs the jobs prune. Exits 0 when it removed what was older than the last three releases; 1 when a release could not be removed. Started again: never.

## 7. Deployment and implementation

### Environments

| Environment | Purpose | Run by | Promotes to |
|---|---|---|---|
| production | The host whose services the watcher keeps current. | vendor |   |

### Configuration

| Setting | Type | Secret | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| registryAddress | string |   | The address of the registry the watcher asks for new releases. |
| registryToken | string | yes | The token the watcher reads the registry with, from the environment file only root reads. |
| logLevel | string |   | How much the watcher logs. |

### Monitors

What is watched on the live system, and the objective each must meet.

| Monitor | Environment | Measures | Objective | Verifies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| watcher-running | production | Whether the release watcher's unit is active. | The unit is active at every check, each minute of the day. | RW-2 |

### Implementation: Release watcher in Go, under systemd

From the implementation file version 1.0.0.

One Go program for both processes, run by the systemd units in
../sources/units: the daemon for releaseWatcher, and the same program
with the argument prune for releasePrune.

Stack: language Go 1.26.

## 10. Quality requirements

The design tests: what must hold on every implementation. Golden scenarios succeed; red scenarios are refused.

| Test | Subject | Level | Scenario | Given | When | Then |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| prune-release-running | job prune | system | red | the oldest of four releases of a service is the one running | the job prune runs | it keeps the running release and removes the oldest of the others |
| prune-runs-twice | job prune | system | golden | the job prune has run and three releases of each service are left | it runs again over the same records | nothing changes a second time |
| prune-succeeds | job prune | system | golden | four releases of a service are on disk | the job prune runs | the oldest is removed and the last three are kept |
| release-prune-exit-1 | process releasePrune | system | red | a release directory the program cannot remove | the process releasePrune ends | it exits 1: a release could not be removed |
| release-prune-succeeds | process releasePrune | system | golden | four releases of a service are on disk | the process releasePrune is started at 03:00 UTC, when the job prune is due | it does its work and exits 0: it removed what was older than the last three releases |
| release-watcher-crash-loop-given-up | process releaseWatcher | system | red | the process releaseWatcher fails each time it starts | it has been started 5 times within PT10M | the service manager does not start it again, and the monitor watcher-running alerts |
| release-watcher-exit-78 | process releaseWatcher | system | red | the setting registryAddress is not a URI | the process releaseWatcher ends | it exits 78 and the service manager does not start it again |
| release-watcher-restarted-after-a-crash | process releaseWatcher | system | red | the process releaseWatcher is running | it ends with status 1 | the service manager starts it again after PT5S |
| release-watcher-secret-missing-registry-token | process releaseWatcher | system | red | the secret registryToken is missing | the process releaseWatcher starts | it exits 78 before it asks the registry, naming registryToken |
| release-watcher-setting-invalid-log-level | process releaseWatcher | system | red | the setting logLevel is verbose, which is not one of error, info and debug | the process releaseWatcher starts | it exits 78 before it asks the registry, naming logLevel |
| release-watcher-setting-invalid-registry-address | process releaseWatcher | system | red | the setting registryAddress is missing | the process releaseWatcher starts | it exits 78 before it asks the registry, naming registryAddress |
| release-watcher-signal-sighup | process releaseWatcher | system | golden | the process releaseWatcher is running and logLevel has changed to debug | it receives SIGHUP | it reads its settings again and logs at debug, without a restart |
| release-watcher-signal-sigterm | process releaseWatcher | system | golden | the process releaseWatcher is installing a release | it receives SIGTERM | it finishes that release, then exits 0, within PT30S |
| release-watcher-succeeds | process releaseWatcher | system | golden | its settings are valid and a new release is in the registry | the process releaseWatcher starts | it is healthy: it asks the registry each minute, tells the service manager so, and installs the new release within two minutes |
| rw-2-acceptance-1 | requirement RW-2 | acceptance | golden | the release watcher is running | it is killed with SIGKILL | it runs again within five seconds |
| rw-2-acceptance-2 | requirement RW-2 | acceptance | golden | the release watcher's registryAddress names a host that refuses every connection, so each run fails | it has failed five times within ten minutes | it stays stopped and the monitor watcher-running alerts |
| sweep-registry-down | job sweep | system | red | the registry does not answer | the job sweep runs | it installs nothing, logs the error, and asks again on its next run |
| sweep-runs-twice | job sweep | system | golden | the job sweep has installed release 1.4.0 | it runs again and the registry still holds 1.4.0 | it installs nothing a second time |
| sweep-succeeds | job sweep | system | golden | the registry holds release 1.4.0 of a service and 1.3.0 is installed | the job sweep runs | it installs 1.4.0 |

## 13. Requirements

### Needs

| Need | Statement | Stakeholders | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| NEED-1 | The host's services run their latest release without a person installing each one. | host-owner | accepted |

### Requirements

| Requirement | Statement | Kind | Priority | Status | Verification | Acceptance | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RW-1 | The release watcher shall install a new release of a service within two minutes of its publication in the registry. | functional | must | accepted | test | A release published while the watcher runs is installed within two minutes. | NEED-1 |
| RW-2 | The release watcher shall come back after a crash, and a person shall be told when it stops for good. | functional | must | accepted | test | After a crash the watcher runs again within five seconds. After five crashes within ten minutes it stays stopped and the monitor watcher-running alerts. | NEED-1 |
| RW-3 | The host shall keep the last three releases of each service and no more. | functional | should | accepted | test | After the nightly prune each service has at most three releases on disk. | NEED-1 |
